A1.justification: Both PDFs present FMCPE with the same two-flow construction and four core benchmarks. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the title change and substantial expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Gaussian, Pendulum, Wind Tunnel and Light Tunnel tasks, including quantitative comparisons and posterior visualizations in Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark experiments and adds calibration diagnostics, component ablations, prior-misspecification experiments, timing measurements and hyperparameter studies.

M1.justification: The two transports, simulation-informed source distribution, flow-matching losses, joint optimization, frozen posterior estimator and stop-gradient sampling procedure remain equivalent in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The broader prior assumptions and additional implementation disclosures do not establish a changed FMCPE algorithm.

E1.justification: The four original tasks remain, but Appendices D.3–D.4 add materially different test scenarios: controlled violations of conditional independence and prior misspecification in Gaussian and Wind Tunnel models. The latter includes training under a restricted [10,20] prior while targeting [0,45], substantially extending the parameter populations and mismatch conditions evaluated.

E2.justification: v1 explicitly excludes RoPE and compares against NPE and MFNPE. v5 adds RoPE to the main comparisons and evaluates NNPE and J-NPE in Appendix D.1, Figures 6–7. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Gaussian evaluation changes from joint-distribution jC2ST and Wasserstein metrics to conditional-posterior metrics averaged over three observations. v5 also introduces MMD, SBC using 1,000 pairs and 500 posterior draws per pair, a fixed-budget hyperparameter grid, and inference timing over 5,000 observations. These are substantive evaluation changes and new protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's calibration-size comparisons and posterior examples, v5 tests joint versus sequential training, each transport separately, dependence on conditional independence, robustness to prior misspecification, and learning-rate/clipping sensitivity. Figures 10–13 additionally compare posteriors before and after correction. These directly investigate previously untested design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: The original five-calibration-set boxplots remain. Added analyses report means and standard deviations over three seeds or calibration draws, while SBC explicitly uses one training seed and displays 95% reference bands under uniform ranks. These extend statistical reporting without establishing an increase in the original experiments' run counts.

E6.justification: v5 adds extensive baseline, calibration, robustness, timing and sensitivity results. For example, Table 1 reports jC2ST 0.768 ± 0.041 for full FMCPE versus 0.864 ± 0.004 for TX-only at dependence strength α = 2. Gaussian scores use changed metrics, preventing direct version-to-version performance comparison, and v1's Gaussian MSE panel is absent. Wind Tunnel KDE curve assignments for NPE and MFNPE also swap between v1 Figure 5 and v5 Figure 8.

T1.justification: v5 relaxes the known-correct-prior premise to allow an approximate training prior qΘ. New Appendix A derives a Gaussian counterexample showing persistent physical-parameter bias despite an M-closed model, and Section 3.2 adds a conditional-independence condition for identifying qX|Y with pX|Y. The central transport derivations remain unchanged; no new correction-error guarantee is established.

C1.justification: The central contribution—amortized posterior correction using scarce calibration data and two flows—is retained. The abstract and introduction extend its stated scope explicitly to prior and noise misspecification, including uncertainty about which model component is wrong. This is a scope extension within the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v5 interprets ablations as supporting joint source/posterior adaptation, attributes RoPE's uniform SBC ranks to prior regularization, and discusses persistent Wind Tunnel miscalibration and SBC's inability to guarantee correctness. It also identifies ODE sampling costs and missing calibration-size bounds. These substantially expand v1's interpretation and limitations, although Appendix C reverses the dispersion interpretations of U-shaped and hump-shaped rank histograms.

D1.justification: v5 replaces the supplementary-ZIP disclosure with a repository link and adds the UMNN implementation reference, Pendulum noise scale, Gaussian seed-recovery instructions, explicit-Euler solver disclosure, default learning rate and clipping threshold, and detailed runtime breakdowns. This substantially improves documented reproducibility without demonstrating that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands research positioning by distinguishing classical M-open/M-closed misspecification from recovery of physically meaningful parameters. It adds discussion of Bernardo and Smith, Bürkner et al., Nott et al. and newer robustness literature, and recognizes Senouf et al.'s inductive alternative to RoPE. MFNPE's publication update does not constitute a new cited method.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially revised; the joint-training explanation is reorganized; and results gain separate comparison, ablation and timing discussions. The original two appendices are reorganized into dedicated sections covering conceptual background, setup, calibration, additional results, timing and sensitivity. These changes materially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, and the overview moves to the first page. Benchmark plots gain comparators and revised Gaussian metric labels; existing posterior plots are relocated or revised. New SBC grids, correction visualizations, ablation and sensitivity plots, and numerical tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked component ablations, excluded the closely related RoPE comparator, and provided only coarse computational-cost information. v5 directly addresses these gaps through broader comparisons, tests of both flows and joint training, prior-shift experiments, and measured runtime breakdowns. This substantially strengthens support for the method's design and practical applicability. The reversed SBC dispersion labels and overly broad clipping-robustness interpretation require correction, but these reporting problems do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
